reason: This is the only available action, and it should start the crane’s winding mechanism.
expectation: I expect the crank and ratchet wheel to attach to the drum, though I’m not yet sure how the holding mechanism will work.

effect: The winch winds cord, and its longer crank trades hand travel for more turning effect. It now needs mounting.
reaction: The trade-off is a useful detail.
reason: Mounting the winch is the only offered combination and should advance the crane.
expectation: I expect the hand winch to attach to the crane frame, ready for the lifting cord.

effect: The winch is mounted, so the crane can now be fitted with its lifting cord.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should connect the winch to a load.
expectation: I expect the cord and hook to be fitted to the crane, probably running over the tip pulley.

effect: The lifting line is fitted, so the crane is ready for a test load.
reason: The padded weight is the only offered combination and should test the lifting setup.
expectation: I expect to try lifting the weight and possibly learn whether the crane is stable.

effect: The frame is stiff, but the test shows the whole crane tends to tip forward; it needs counterweight at the rear.
reaction: The distinction between bending and tipping is useful and clear.
reason: The rear ballast is the only offered combination and should counter the load’s tipping effect.
expectation: I expect the ballast to help keep the back feet down during another low test, though it may not address holding the load.

effect: The rear ballast keeps the feet down during the repeated low lift; holding the load remains to be addressed.
reaction: The repeat test makes the ballast’s purpose clear.
reason: The pawl and release lever are the only offered combination and should help hold and lower the load.
expectation: I expect the pawl to engage the ratchet to prevent unwinding, with the lever allowing a controlled release.

effect: The pawl holds the drum when winding stops; lowering requires holding the crank while easing the release lever.
reaction: The explanation makes the holding and release mechanism clear.
reason: The basket is the only offered combination and should let me test the crane’s intended load.
expectation: I expect to lift, hold and gently lower the basket using the winch and pawl.

effect: The basket test confirmed that the pawl holds the load and that the crane can lower it onto the platform under control. The chapter goal is complete.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the separate mechanisms work together for a delivery.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the weight and seeing the back feet lift was most worthwhile: it made the difference between a stiff frame and a stable crane concrete.

leastWorthwhile.text: Mounting the winch was a straightforward assembly step without much to consider, especially as it was the only offered combination.

surprise.text: The frame stayed stiff while the whole crane tried to tip; the rear ballast then kept its feet down in the repeat test.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although the single available combination at each decision left little room for meaningful choice.

continue.text: I would continue for another chapter: the test-and-fix sequence made the crane’s mechanics understandable, though I would hope for more decisions.
